messages:
chris-cust: Customer reports intermittent 502s + TLS timeouts when calling Redwood private API via an interface endpoint after they changed route tables. Happens only from their VPC; public access fine. curl inside VPC: "curl: (35) SSL_read: errno=0". Gateway logs show upstream SSL handshake failures and 502s. Any quick triage?
sara-support: What region, endpoint details, sample request-id and exact RTB change? :eyes:
chris-cust: Region us-west-2. Endpoint service: com.redwood.api (interface). Subnets: subnet-0a1b2c3d (az-a), subnet-0d3c2b1a (az-b). They associated route-table rtb-08f1 to those subnets last night. Sample request-id: rq_3f7a2b. Repro from customer: 1) dig +short internal-api.redwood.prod -> 10.2.1.45 (ENI) 2) curl -v https://internal-api.redwood.prod/health -> times out / 502 intermittently 3) traceroute to 10.2.1.45 shows next-hop = tgw-0zzzz (expected local VPC). Logs: "upstream_ssl_handshake: tlsv1.3 handshake failure (sni mismatch?) from 10.2.1.45". Also they've seen a billing spike on tokens due to retries.
mike-platform: My bet: route table precedence means their RTB has a TGW route that captures traffic to the ENI IPs. Interface endpoints require return path to be local (ENI). If reply traffic leaves via TGW you get asymmetric routing, TLS failures (SNI/source IP mismatch) and intermittent 502s. Quick checks: 
- aws ec2 describe-route-tables --route-table-ids rtb-08f1 --region us-west-2
- aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters "Name=attachment.instance-owner-id,Values=vpce-*" --region us-west-2
Also confirm source/dest check on endpoint ENIs is enabled and that there is no upstream NAT gateway or firewall rewriting connections.
natalie-eng-sre: Another angle: split-horizon private hosted zone (PHZ) collisions. If they have overlapping PHZs or resolver rules, DNS might resolve to a different private IP (or an NLB behind TGW). Run: 
```
dig +trace internal-api.redwood.prod @169.254.169.253
```
and compare to dig from a non-VPC host. Also verify the endpoint "Enable private DNS name" setting.
chris-cust: Ran checks with customer and findings: 
- describe-route-tables: rtb-08f1 contains route 10.2.0.0/16 -> tgw-0zzzz (attached to endpoint subnets)
- describe-network-interfaces: vpce ENIs present with IPs 10.2.1.45 & 10.2.2.12
- dig inside VPC resolves to 10.2.1.45 (so DNS points to ENI) but traceroute exits to TGW due to RTB entry. They added TGW route earlier for cross-account routing.
They ran openssl: 
```
openssl s_client -connect 10.2.1.45:443 -servername internal-api.redwood.prod -quiet
# handshake stalls then EOF; certificate presented looks odd when compared to public interaction
```
This points to asymmetric path or an inline proxy/firewall altering the handshake.
sara-support: Immediate mitigation suggestions to pass on: 
1) Re-associate endpoint subnets to an RTB that doesn't contain the broad TGW route, or remove the TGW route from rtb-08f1.
2) If RTB change not possible immediately, add more-specific /32 routes for the ENI IPs (10.2.1.45/32, 10.2.2.12/32) -> local.
3) Temporarily allow outbound 443 to our hosted egress IP ranges (confirm exact list on support portal) to avoid TLS stripping by inline devices. Example ranges (customer must verify): ["54.39.32.0/24", "54.40.16.0/24"].
mike-platform: Repro plan if SRE needs to replicate: 
1) Provision VPC + TGW. 
2) Create interface endpoint in a subnet that uses a RTB with a TGW route for the VPC CIDR. 
3) From an EC2 in the same subnet curl the private DNS -> observe intermittent 502 / TLS handshake failures.
natalie-eng-sre: Root cause summary: TGW route attached to endpoint subnets caused asymmetric routing. Client SYN reaches endpoint ENI; backend reply exits via TGW and is dropped or altered en route, causing incomplete TLS handshakes and 502s. Retries amplify billing/requests. Long-term recommendations: 
- Avoid attaching TGW/default-propagated routes to endpoint subnets. Use dedicated service subnets or explicit more-specific routes for endpoint ENIs.
- Enforce RTB hygiene via IaC + pre-deploy checks.
- Ensure PHZs do not collide; use resolver rules for cross-account lookups.
- Add monitoring: alert when traceroute to ENI IPs shows non-local next-hop or when gateway logs report upstream_ssl_handshake errors.
chris-cust: Passed mitigations to customer; they removed the TGW route from rtb-08f1 and 502/TLS errors stopped immediately. They asked for a write-up to include commands and preventive checklist for their network team.
sara-support: I'll draft a KB with commands, repro steps, egress allowlist note, and RTB hygiene checklist; tagging @natalie-eng-sre for SRE postmortem checklist. :thumbsup:
natalie-eng-sre: Will draft postmortem checklist including: route table audit commands, PHZ collision detection, DNS validation commands, traceroute diagnostics, and recommended IaC guardrails. I can drop a runbook in /docs/runbooks/vpce-routing on confluence. :white_check_mark:
infra-bot: deploy-log: KB draft created at https://confluence.redwood.ai/kb/vpce-route-asymmetry by sara-support
chris-cust: Customer confirmed billing spike is recoverable and they're satisfied. Marking resolved. :rocket:
